payload.name: Verify existing memory before redundant SKIP
payload.description: When deciding to SKIP a candidate because it duplicates an existing memory, first confirm that the existing memory is actually present in the retrieved memory pool and covers the candidate fact.
content: Before applying SKIP due to redundancy, verify that the referenced existing memory is present in the retrieved memory pool and semantically covers the candidate's key fact.
If no such memory exists in the retrieved pool, do not SKIP; ADD the candidate as a new memory (or apply the appropriate UPDATE/MERGE).
Do not assume redundancy from conversation context, earlier turns, or memories not actually retrieved in the current decision stage.

solves: During construction decision, candidates may be SKIPped as redundant based on an assumed existing memory even when the retrieved memory pool contains no such memory. This rule applies whenever a SKIP reason cites coverage by an existing memory: require that memory to be present in the retrieved pool and to actually cover the candidate fact before skipping.
